_comment: The E2E specs worth running on a REAL Windows / macOS runner, consumed by
Selection rule: a spec earns a place here only if Linux genuinely cannot
validate it — it reads bytes back off disk, drives OS integration, or loads
a per-platform native binary. The other ~96 specs are renderer maths or
identical Python and are fully covered by ci.yml; running them three times
would triple the wall clock for no signal.
PREFER NOT ADDING TO THIS LIST. Anything expressible as a pure function over
a platform string belongs in a unit test instead, where the free Linux
runner checks all three platforms in about a second — see
That bug (the octree cache reader and writer disagreeing on Windows and
Linux, with macOS passing only because APFS is case-insensitive) is the
archetype: it is caught by a contract test, not by cross-OS E2E.

groups.why: Backend supervision and the octree cache root — the class of bug that shipped broken on Windows and Linux while macOS passed by accident.
OS integration that has no Linux equivalent: the macOS app menu vs the Windows menubar, the real file dialogs, and Electron's webUtils.getPathForFile drag-drop path.

Export round-trips, one per format family. These write real files and read the bytes back, so they are where path separators, drive letters and text-mode newline translation surface. Note main.py writes XML and the ASCII hits-only copy with open(path, 'w') and no newline='', which becomes CRLF on Windows.

Imports that go through per-platform native wheels (laspy/lazrs, pye57, plyfile) or resolve relative asset paths. import-material-obj covers MTL and texture resolution, which is separator-sensitive; import-sbet-trajectory covers pyproj, whose bundled PROJ data directory is a classic per-platform packaging failure.
PotreeConverter is a separately-built external binary per platform, invoked as a subprocess.
Proof that the native libraries actually load and compute from inside the packaged layout: libhelios (.dll/.dylib) with its lidar and plantarchitecture plugins, and the CSF C-extension.
